stated: Review assessment targets to treat arts and vocational subjects equally, support outdoor play and learning, include climate and biodiversity crisis education, ensure effective delivery of the Natural History GCSE, and end high-stakes formal testing.

source.quote: Elected Greens will: • Review assessment targets in schools so that arts and vocational subjects are treated equally within the curriculum, children are supported to play and learn outdoors, and every child can learn about the climate and biodiversity crisis to equip them for the challenges ahead. • Ensure effective delivery of the new Natural History GCSE. • Reduces the stress in our education system by ending high-stakes, formal testing at primary and secondary schools and by abolishing OFSTED.

bearing_set.reason: Directly reshapes school curriculum, assessment structures, and subject parity — all core indicators of school standards, attainment, and opportunity for pupils.

membership_note: O6 is not in the bearing-set: including climate/biodiversity as curriculum content educates about the environment but does not itself move emissions, air quality, or biodiversity indicators — the effect on O6 is too indirect and speculative. O14 (attainment gap/inequality) is a genuine sub-indicator within O7 rather than a separate material bearing on wealth/income inequality. No other fundamental is mechanistically moved by this curriculum and assessment reform.
